Pippit vs VEXI: Creative Tool or Your Whole Social Media?
Pippit and VEXI, side by side: what each one does and what it costs, from each company's own pages.
Pippit is an AI creative tool powered by CapCut, with a publisher and a social calendar [1][4]. Here is how it compares with one app that makes your posts and runs your week.

Pippit is an AI creative tool, and its home page says it is “Powered by CapCut” [1]. It turns any link, file or media into videos, designs posters, social media posts and ads, and makes digital avatar and AI talking-photo videos [1]. Its AI video editor changes an uploaded clip from instructions you type [3]. Its Publisher schedules posts on a social calendar to TikTok, Facebook and Instagram [4][5]. Its pricing page lists a USD0 plan with free daily credits, and paid Starter, Plus and Pro plans with monthly credits; on the yearly view today, Starter is USD101 a year and Plus is USD246 a year [2].

VEXI is an AI content studio that runs social media for entrepreneurs and creators. You describe what you want and it makes the posts, videos, designs and captions, then schedules and publishes them. Plans start at $199 a month, and every plan starts with a 15-day trial.

Credit where it is due: Pippit makes a lot, and schedules it [1][5]. The difference is who does the work. In Pippit you pick the tool, type what you want, and schedule each post on its calendar [3][5]. VEXI does that: your own clips come back with B-roll, music and captions, the posts come back designed and captioned, and Autopilot runs your week. VEXI costs more than Pippit: plans are $199, $399 or $599 a month [2]. What you pay for is the work you no longer do.
In Pippit's AI video editor you upload a clip and type the changes you want, and you can split and trim it and add captions, music and stock footage [3].
Send VEXI the clips you shot and they come back cut, with B-roll, music and captions, sized for each platform.
Pippit's help center says it currently supports posting to TikTok, Facebook and Instagram [4].
VEXI posts to Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn, Pinterest, Threads and your Google Business Profile.
Pippit's Publisher puts the posts you schedule on a social calendar, and you can plan up to 30 days ahead in its monthly view [4][5].
VEXI Autopilot runs your week ahead: it writes, cuts and posts, and can wait for your approval on everything.
Edits your own footage: cuts, B-roll, music, captions
A broad AI toolbox powered by CapCut, with video, image and avatar tools and a publisher for TikTok, Facebook and Instagram [1][4].
One app: you ask, and it writes, designs, edits the video and posts it. Autopilot runs your week ahead.

Pippit is an AI creative tool, and its home page says it is “Powered by CapCut” [1]. It makes videos from links and media, avatar and talking-photo videos and image designs, and it can schedule posts [1][5]. Its site is pippit.ai [1].
Does Pippit post to social media?

Yes: Pippit's help center says it currently supports posting to TikTok, Facebook and Instagram, on a schedule you set in its calendar [4]. VEXI posts to Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn, Pinterest, Threads and your Google Business Profile, and Autopilot can run the week.
Can Pippit edit my own videos?

Yes: in Pippit's AI video editor you upload a clip and type the changes you want, and you can add captions, music and stock footage [3]. VEXI edits your footage for you: cuts, B-roll, music and captions.

Pippit's pricing page lists a USD0 plan with free daily credits, and paid Starter, Plus and Pro plans that come with monthly credits [2]. On the yearly view today, Starter is USD101 a year (USD168 shown beside it), Plus is USD246 a year (USD410) and Pro is USD2,196 a year (USD3,660) [2]. Its pricing page says plans auto renew and you can cancel anytime [2].
